cranium.name: Skull (cranium and face)
cranium.description: Eight cranial bones fused into a box that protects the brain, and thirteen face bones (the lower jaw is shown separately). They meet at immovable joints called sutures.

mandible.name: Lower jaw (mandible)
mandible.description: The only bone of the skull that moves, at a hinge joint in front of each ear, for chewing and speaking.

hyoid.name: Hyoid bone
hyoid.description: A small U-shaped bone in the neck below the jaw. It touches no other bone; the tongue's muscles are attached to it.

cervical_vertebrae.name: Neck vertebrae (cervical, 7)
cervical_vertebrae.description: The seven vertebrae of the neck. The first two, the atlas and the axis, form the pivot joint that lets the head turn from side to side.

thoracic_vertebrae.name: Chest vertebrae (thoracic, 12)
thoracic_vertebrae.description: The twelve vertebrae of the chest. Each pair of ribs is joined to one of them at the back.

lumbar_vertebrae.name: Lower back vertebrae (lumbar, 5)
lumbar_vertebrae.description: The five largest vertebrae, in the lower back. They carry the weight of the whole upper body.

sacrum.name: Sacrum
sacrum.description: Five vertebrae fused into one triangular bone at the base of the spine. It joins the two hip bones to make the pelvis.

intervertebral_discs.name: Discs between the vertebrae (cartilage)
intervertebral_discs.description: Pads of cartilage between the vertebrae. They cushion the spine and let it bend, a little at each joint.

ribs.name: Ribs (12 pairs)
ribs.description: Twelve pairs of curved bones that protect the heart and lungs. The top seven pairs join the breastbone directly (true ribs), the next three join it through cartilage (false ribs), and the last two are free at the front (floating ribs).

sternum.name: Breastbone (sternum)
sternum.description: The flat bone at the front of the chest, where the ribs meet. It is made of three pieces: the manubrium, the body and the xiphoid process.

costal_cartilages.name: Rib cartilages (costal)
costal_cartilages.description: Bars of cartilage joining the ribs to the breastbone. Being flexible, they let the chest rise and fall when we breathe.

clavicle.name: Collarbone (clavicle) (right and left)
clavicle.description: A long S-shaped bone across the top of the chest, from the breastbone to the shoulder. It holds the arm out from the body.

scapula.name: Shoulder blade (scapula) (right and left)
scapula.description: A flat triangular bone at the back of the shoulder. Its shallow socket takes the head of the humerus at the shoulder's ball-and-socket joint.

humerus.name: Upper arm bone (humerus) (right and left)
humerus.description: The long bone of the upper arm, from the shoulder to the elbow.

radius.name: Radius (right and left)
radius.description: The forearm bone on the thumb side. It rolls round the ulna to turn the palm up or down.

ulna.name: Ulna (right and left)
ulna.description: The forearm bone on the little-finger side. Its hooked top end makes the point of the elbow and the elbow's hinge joint.

carpals.name: Wrist bones (carpals, 8 each) (right and left)
carpals.description: Eight small bones in two rows at the wrist, which glide over one another so the wrist can bend and turn.

metacarpals.name: Palm bones (metacarpals, 5 each) (right and left)
metacarpals.description: Five long bones in the palm, one leading to each finger.

hand_phalanges.name: Finger bones (phalanges, 14 each) (right and left)
hand_phalanges.description: Three bones in each finger and two in the thumb, joined by hinge joints.

hip_bone.name: Hip bone (pelvic girdle) (right and left)
hip_bone.description: Each hip bone is three bones fused together (ilium, ischium and pubis). With the sacrum they make the pelvis, which holds up the organs of the abdomen. Its deep socket takes the head of the femur at the hip's ball-and-socket joint.

femur.name: Thigh bone (femur) (right and left)
femur.description: The longest and strongest bone in the body, from the hip to the knee.

patella.name: Kneecap (patella) (right and left)
patella.description: A small flat bone at the front of the knee, inside the tendon of the thigh muscle. It protects the knee joint.

tibia.name: Shin bone (tibia) (right and left)
tibia.description: The larger bone of the lower leg, on the inner side. It carries the body's weight from the knee to the ankle.

fibula.name: Fibula (right and left)
fibula.description: The thin bone on the outer side of the lower leg. It carries little weight; muscles are attached to it, and its lower end makes the outer bump of the ankle.

tarsals.name: Ankle and heel bones (tarsals, 7 each) (right and left)
tarsals.description: Seven bones at the ankle and the back of the foot. The largest, the calcaneus, is the heel; the talus joins the foot to the leg.

metatarsals.name: Foot bones (metatarsals, 5 each) (right and left)
metatarsals.description: Five long bones in the middle of the foot, one leading to each toe. With the tarsals they make the arch of the foot.

foot_phalanges.name: Toe bones (phalanges, 14 each) (right and left)
foot_phalanges.description: Three bones in each toe and two in the big toe.

coccyx.name: Tailbone (coccyx)
coccyx.note: BodyParts3D does not model the coccyx, the four tiny fused vertebrae below the sacrum. It can be explained but not shown.

ear_ossicles.name: Ear bones (ossicles)
ear_ossicles.note: The three tiny bones of each middle ear (hammer, anvil, stirrup) are not in BodyParts3D. The stapes is the smallest bone in the body, about 3 mm long.

notes: 199 of the 206 bones of an adult: BodyParts3D has no coccyx and no ear ossicles. The backbone's regions are tinted apart and cartilage is shown bluish-white, a teaching convention; real bone is all one colour.
